resources.string: Show this phone\'s screen on your computer
Your computer can ask to show this screen in a window. Each time, your phone asks you first.
Taps, swipes, Back, Home, Recents and typing from the computer\'s window, while you share your screen with it.
Android carries out the computer\'s taps and typing through link2linux\'s accessibility service. In Accessibility settings, open link2linux control and turn it on.
If Android says the setting is restricted, which it does for apps installed from outside an app store: open App info, tap the three-dot menu, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Control is on while you share your screen.

When a computer asks to see your screen, your phone asks you first, every time, and names the computer. Android then shows that your screen is shared. To stop, tap Stop sharing in the notification, or close the window on the computer. Locking your phone also stops it. Android hides some things from shared screens, such as passwords and the content of notifications. The computer shows your screen only in its window and does not record it.
Allow notifications, so that your phone can ask you when link2linux is in the background.

link2linux uses an Android accessibility service to carry out what you do in your computer's window: taps, swipes, Back, Home, Recents, opening the notifications, and typing.

It does this only while you share your screen with that computer and this switch is on. To type, it looks up the text field that has the focus and its text, and changes only that field. It reads nothing else on the screen, and it stores and sends nothing: your computer sees the screen through screen sharing, not through this service.

Next, Android's Accessibility settings open: turn on link2linux control there. You can turn it off there or here at any time.
